original_acceptance: Deltas link both source revisions and distinguish absent from unknown/incomparable fields.
Duplicate input cannot manufacture duplicate semantic changes.
Consumers can replay the provided sequences and understand each change reason.
Every listed artifact exists or has an agreed equivalent path, and an independent reviewer can reproduce the documented procedure.
Record actual tests, input/configuration revisions and unresolved failures; planned/reference examples do not establish completion.

asset_research_plan.decision: Produce field-level asset changes from immutable observations, with explicit collection completeness and ordering, so consumers can distinguish a real removal from failed collection.
questions: Which package/service/OS changes are comparable across collector versions and incomplete snapshots?
How should duplicates, late arrivals, time skew and missing fields affect a delta?
Which inventory events can D13 consume without mistaking a failed collection for an uninstall?
asset_research_plan.comparison: Define a delta contract linking two immutable snapshot IDs, asset identity and comparison revision.
cases: A partial/failed package listing must not imply all prior packages were removed.
Reorder and duplicate snapshots; preserve stable event identity and explain chronology conflicts.
Verify that raw evidence stays unchanged and D13 can consume the delta fixture without a new scheduler.
consumers: C19: comparable snapshot history for evidence-quality evaluation.
C22/C23: replayable changes for contribution tests and observed service relationships.
D13: optional asset-change event input; Mahrous retains impact analysis and reassessment scheduling.
asset_research_plan.reviewers: Mahrous reviews the D13 event boundary; Omar reviews existing event/persistence compatibility.
asset_research_plan.start: Post-first-slice: complete C17, C05 first; draft research/fixtures earlier without claiming measured completion.
